criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: This is a bespoke LOOK V2 deck, and the nine frames really are different pictures: a rack, a counter, a cold aisle, a relief page, a dusk room, a chamber, a macro shot, a sorter and a desk. Colour is vivid and nowhere near black (preflight median chroma 57.7, 37.0 and 52.3 on slides 1, 5 and 9). S5 is the strongest frame. Both stacks read as wrapped paper, I count 3 reams plus a loose block against 8 reams plus a torn top, and machine_qa measures hpx 241.5 against 531.6, ratio 2.2013 against truth 2.2013, err 0. S4 is a real TXBENCH relief (height_range 75.95, 12 materials, cast_fraction 0.95) with three raised wax seals. S8 has exactly 6x5 = 30 cubbies with the lit last one. What holds the score down: on S7, the frame the storyboard names as its showstopper, the stack is a smeared stripe blob and the page is greeked dashes, so no subject is sharp at 432 px, and machine_qa flags both text blocks outside the 80 px safe zone. On S2 the table grain is a motion-blur streak and the objects sit small in the lower half under a flat violet top. On S6 the two piles are crowded at the bottom edge under the dek while the flags and seal take the focus. On S8 the sorter is clean but generic CG with flat cards. S5's rule is a flat lilac strip square to camera (the reviewer's own note).

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: The spine holds: one violet, rose and kraft palette, one serif and sans pair, an mm counter and a cite line on every frame, and the dusk gold accent kept to the words of the proposal (S1 clipped line, S4 paragraph, S7 line, S8 tab, S9 letter line). It never touches a stack. On the contact sheet the paper motif runs 1, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9 as a real changing motif. S2 (red-brown smeared table) and S6 (orange-red chamber) sit a little warm and outside the rest, and the S9 stack's olive-kraft wrappers are flatter than S5's, which weakens the claim that it is the same stack.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: I checked every numeral against figures.json and claims.json. $1,947,310,000 (c26), $4,286,040,000 (c31), $507,450,000 (c32), $1,116,890,000 (c37), $4.3 billion (state_fy2032_bn, half up), 1987 (c7), 30 days (c41), 3.308 (c4), and December 20th (c43, and computed as Nov 20 + 30 = Dec 20). Caption January 1st and August 1st trace to c17 and c15. 'Rises in each year it counts' is true: c26 to c31 run 1.947, 2.272, 2.655, 3.108, 3.646, 4.286, all cited on S5. compute.py extracts every value by regex from claim quotes. Slide sources are primary (the Texas Register and the comptroller release). The Tribune carries only the Eckhardt lines in the caption, and those are listed in first_comment. Looseness found: (1) S1 and the caption say Huffines 'proposed' on November 18th, but c2 says he 'announced' that day, c42 has it filed November 9th and c45 published November 20th. The verb is looser than its source. (2) S7 credits the finding to 'the chief revenue estimator', but that attribution is in c38's paraphrase text, not in its verbatim quote string. (3) S6's two piles and S9's stack carry no year or scale on the frame, so a reader can't check the drawing against a figure there, and the S1 rack, S6 chamber and S9 desk are illustrative without the 'drawn to illustrate' note S3 carries. None of these changes what a reader believes about the rule or the money.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: The deck names the decider (Comptroller Don Huffines), the instrument (Rule 3.308, Texas Register November 20th), the change (cloud, AI and quantum classed as hosted technology services, outside the tax), the state and local stakes in dollars, the 30-day window, the earliest adoption date, and a named contact with an email (S9). It is clearly marked as a proposal (S9 headline, caption 'Nothing is adopted yet'). Short of 10: S9 says 'Mail or email' but leaves off the P.O. Box 13528, Austin 78711 address that c40 holds, so the mail option can't be acted on from the deck. The handover to Eckhardt, which is the real open question, appears only in the caption.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover question earns the swipe and S2 pays at once with the 1987 definition. The turn lands at S5 (the measured stacks) into S7 ('insignificant' against the losses), and S8 and S9 close on an action. S2 and S3 are both definition beats and either could fold into the other without much loss. S6 restates S5's move at a smaller scale.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and within house rules. I found no colons or semicolons in the copy, no dashes, no banned words, and 'can't' is used. The tone is honest without doom. The register is flat and procedural, though: 'The hall is drawn to illustrate', 'Cities, counties and transit authorities are among them'. Nothing reads as a Texan who knows Austin's rulemaking, and nothing local is named, such as which cities or transit authorities depend on this revenue.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The topic is new, and topics.json shows no comptroller or data-processing-tax deck in the 30-day window. The core move repeats recent decks, though: one physical unit per dollar or count, stacked at a declared scale. That was no. 77's wafers per $1M (Nov 14), no. 80's paper towers (Nov 17), no. 71's cards (Nov 7) and no. 63's slotted weights per $10,000 (Oct 30). The dusk gold accent repeats no. 88 (Nov 26), and paper and folders echo no. 87 (Nov 25 manila folders and card files). This is a fresh concept with more than one familiar move.

ship_note: No fault found. The refusal is the round 1 rung only: 7.55 is under 8.0.
named_defects: S1 dek and caption: 'On November 18th ... proposed' is looser than c2 ('announced'). The filing was November 9th (c42) and publication November 20th (c45). Write 'announced' or 'On November 18th Comptroller Don Huffines announced a proposal ...'.
S7: the chief revenue estimator attribution rests on c38's paraphrase, not its verbatim quote. Confirm the string on the Register page or carry it in the quote.
S6 and S9: the stacks carry no year or unit on the frame, so the one-sheet-per-$1M scale can't be checked where it is reused. S6 doesn't say which pile is 2027 and which is 2032.
S9: 'Mail or email' with no mailing address, though c40 holds P.O. Box 13528, Austin, Texas 78711.
S1, S6, S9: illustrative scenes (rack, chamber with flags and a star seal, desk) carry no 'drawn to illustrate' note. Only S3 does, and copy.json's _note says that is deliberate.
S7: machine_qa WARN, headline and dek outside the 80 px safe zone (486,176 530x343 and 488,541 522x200).
one_sentence_fix: Rebuild frame 7 as the deck's real showstopper. Put the fiscal 2032 stack in sharp focus at its true 428.6 mm height, with its 8 reams countable and its shadow falling on a page the reader can recognise. Pull the type inside the safe zone, and label the reused stacks on frames 6 and 9 with their fiscal year, so the one-sheet-per-million scale reads and can be checked on every frame it appears.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The planned showstopper has no sharp subject at feed size. The fiscal 2032 stack is a smeared stripe blob, the page is greeked dashes in violet shade, and both text blocks sit outside the safe zone.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Rack focus onto the stack. Render it sharp with countable kraft reams and the torn top lit by the coral key, drop the page to a soft foreground band with only the dusk gold line in focus, and move the headline inside the 80 px margin.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The table grain is a motion-blur streak, the papers, floppy and report sit small in the lower half, and the top 40 percent is flat violet behind the type.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lower the camera to counter height so the report and papers fill at least half the frame, and replace the streaked texture with real walnut figure under a window key.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The two local-loss piles are crowded at the bottom edge under the dek with no year cue, while the flags and seal take the focus.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Pull the camera in and down so the two piles stand at mid-frame on the dais ledge, with the 2032 pile visibly about 2.2 times the 2027 pile, and crop the flags to the frame edges.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The sorter is clean but generic CG, with 29 identical flat cards and no wear, so it reads as a template object.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Give the cards varied tilt and paper thickness, add bevel highlights and scuffs to the enamel, and push the camera closer on cubby 30 so the lit letter and gold tab own the bottom third.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The steel rule is a flat lilac strip square to camera, with no thickness, while the stacks are turned 30 degrees.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model the rule as brushed steel with an edge face, turn it to the stacks' 30 degree angle, and seat it with a contact shadow on the oak.
